draft.title: What a business is
card: A business is an organisation that brings together resources to provide goods or services to customers. Resources are the things it needs to operate, such as people, equipment, money and materials.
Most businesses aim to make a profit. This means earning more from customers than it costs to run the business.
Not every organisation is run for profit. A not-for-profit organisation, such as a charity, uses any surplus money to pursue its cause instead of paying owners.
A business is defined by what it does: it combines resources to serve customers. Size does not matter. A one-person business and a large company are both businesses.
draft.remember: A business combines resources to serve customers, and usually aims for profit.

a.q: Which description best fits a business?
opts: It combines resources to serve customers with goods or services
It only sells physical goods to customers
It is owned by the government and has no customers
It must employ many staff and operate from a large building
a.why: A business brings together resources to serve customers, usually to make a profit. The option about physical goods is tempting, but businesses can also provide services.
a.clue: Think about what a business does, not how big it is.

b.q: Jas mows lawns in Bathurst. She owns a mower, buys fuel, works alone and charges customers a fee. Why is this a business?
opts: She combines resources to provide a service to customers
She earns money, and that alone makes it a business
She uses a mower, which is a physical good she owns
She has no staff, so she is not part of a larger firm
b.why: Jas combines her labour, mower and fuel to serve customers. Earning money alone is not the test, because a person can earn money without serving customers. Mowing is a service, so owning the mower is not what makes it a business.
b.clue: Look for resources being combined to serve customers.
